correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge9\) the 4-neighborhood tetrahedra Q_i are distinct and intersect in <=2 vertices; the exact explicit free pairs (U_i,Q_i),(E_i,V_i) reduce to the oriented triangulated torus T_n. After a short-edge fault only B_0,A_1 triangle interiors are removed and the surface is genus one with two boundary circles. After a long-edge fault four core triangles and two shared diagonals are removed; dual-graph connectivity supplies elementary collapses of all remaining triangles to a connected graph, and Euler characteristic -2 forces free rank 3. The \(n\ge9\) combinatorial uniqueness assertions have explicit modular formulas; 112 independent finite graph reconstructions and mod-two chain checks plus replayed listed free faces corroborate them, but are not substituted for the all-order proof.

value.rationale: Single-edge resilience of Lovasz neighborhood topology is a structural and naturally motivated question in topological graph theory. The intact squared-cycle neighborhood torus has nontrivial \(H_2\) and rank-two \(H_1\); either inequivalent edge failure destroys its fundamental two-class and creates one extra independent loop, uniformly in the cycle length. The new statement gives a full integral homotopy classification with two explicit, different local puncture mechanisms, beyond numerical f-vector change or a routine consequence of the intact classification.
